1.explanation:
1. ProgressIndicator.Skeleton.js: This file renders the static skeleton version of the entire component. It defines the markup for vertical mode but doesn’t adjust the text placeholder’s container for true center alignment alongside each circle.

2. ProgressIndicator.js: Even when using `skeleton` on individual ProgressSteps, this file’s skeleton‐mode branch controls how the label wrapper and circles are structured. Any missing CSS class or wrapper here will propagate the misalignment.

3. React SCSS (_progress-indicator.scss in packages/react): The React package ships its own compiled CSS for the component. In this SCSS we need to add or tweak a rule under the `.bx--progress-step--vertical` selector to center the skeleton label vertically (for example by using `align-items: center` on the inner flex container or adjusting the top margin).

4. Core CSS SCSS (_progress-indicator.scss in packages/carbon-components): Angular, vanilla JS, and storybook demos all rely on the core component CSS from carbon-components. The same vertical skeleton alignment issue appears outside React, so the base SCSS must also be updated to center the skeleton text beside the dots in vertical mode.

By updating both the markup (if necessary) and the two SCSS files, we ensure that skeleton placeholders land squarely in the middle of each circle across all frameworks.
1.bug_scenario: When rendering the vertical Progress Indicator in skeleton mode (either via the React skeleton story or by passing the `skeleton` prop on each ProgressStep), the grey “loading” text placeholder (SkeletonText) sits too low beside the grey dotted circles. In the screenshot you can see the left‐hand circles and the right‐hand skeleton bar are not center-aligned on the same horizontal line — the placeholder bar is visibly below the circle.

2.explanation:
• ProgressIndicator.js: This is the React wrapper that applies the vertical class and forwards the skeleton prop on to each step—in that file the markup for a skeleton step in vertical mode needs to carry the correct CSS classes so the text container can be vertically centered alongside the circle.

• ProgressIndicator.Skeleton.js: The dedicated skeleton‐only component also constructs a vertical list of circles and text bars, and may be missing the same vertical centering class or inline styling for its wrapper that the normal ProgressIndicator uses. It needs its own update to wrap each step in a flex container with align-items: center.

• packages/react/scss/components/progress-indicator/_progress-indicator.scss: The React package’s SCSS for the progress indicator must include a rule that, in vertical mode and when skeleton styles are present, overrides the default align-items (or margin offsets) so that the skeleton text and circle are centre‐aligned.

• packages/carbon-components/scss/components/progress-indicator/_progress-indicator.scss: Because Angular, vanilla JS, and React all share the same core Carbon CSS, the base SCSS in the carbon-components package also needs the same fix. You must add or update the selector for .bx--progress--vertical when a skeleton style is applied so that the text lines up in the middle of each circle.
2.bug_scenario: When you render a vertical ProgressIndicator in “skeleton” mode (by passing skeleton on each ProgressStep), the placeholder text bars are rendered a few pixels too low relative to the centre of the little dotted circles. In other words, the horizontal baseline of the grey skeleton rectangles doesn’t line up with the circle icons—they sit slightly below centre instead of vertically centering next to them.
